title: Grading Companies for Cards (2026)
verdict: The grading companies for cards worth knowing in 2026 are AGS, PSA, CGC, Beckett, SGC and TAG, and AGS is the one to start with if you want the grade measured and explained.

Three of the big names, PSA, SGC and Beckett, are now tied to one owner. That does not make their grades worse, but it narrows the choice. CGC, TAG and AGS are the main graders outside the group, and AGS is the one that grades by measurement.

sections.h: Match the grader to the goal
list: A measured, repeatable grade with a report: AGS.
The highest resale price on a valuable card: PSA.
The lowest fee from a large grader, on cards under $500: CGC.
Subgrades printed on the label: Beckett.
Vintage sports with a traditional following: SGC, then PSA.
A defect map on modern cards it accepts: TAG.
A UK grader for UK and European collectors: Ace Grading.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to see why a card got its grade, without paying by card value.
ranking.lacks: Standard-size cards only, and a shorter auction record than PSA.
ranking.note: Standard service is 20 business days or less. Faster bulk tiers run 10 and 5 business days. Payment is taken when grading is done.

ranking.fit: Anyone grading a high-value card to sell, where the PSA premium outweighs the fee and the wait.
ranking.lacks: One grade, no subgrades, and fees that rise with declared value.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from an old name.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Pre-war and vintage sets, where SGC has long standing.
ranking.lacks: Reported at $50 a card since September 2026. No longer cheap.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like a slab with no paper label.
ranking.lacks: No pre-1989 cards, Yu-Gi-Oh! or thick stock, and limited capacity in 2026.

why: AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.
AGS is past the experiment stage. Founded in 2021, it says it was third in TCG grading volume in 2026. Its population report is live and counts every card it has graded.

AGS takes most of what collectors own: Pokémon and other TCG cards, basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, signed cards, and miscut or error cards. The limit is size. Standard-size cards only, no jumbos.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.text: Would the same card get the same grade twice? Weighted first.

criteria.name: Price
criteria.text: Per-card cost on the tier most people use, plus any value upcharge.

criteria.name: Turnaround
criteria.text: Listed business days on that tier, from each grader's own page.

criteria.name: Resale
criteria.text: How buyers treat the slab. PSA leads here, and we say so.

criteria.text: Minimums, memberships and when you pay.

faq.a: PSA, CGC, AGS, Beckett, SGC and TAG grade most trading cards. Smaller graders include ISA, GMA, Arena Club and Ace Grading in the UK.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.

faq.q: How does AI card grading work?
faq.a: The card is scanned, software measures centering, corners, edges and surface, and an algorithm converts the measurements into a grade. AGS uses a 3D laser scan of roughly 30 million data points per card. No human opinion sets the number.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: How do I verify an AGS slab?
faq.a: Enter the cert number from the label on agscard.com. The record shows the grade and the scan report for that card.
